package_info.package_name: free-steam-codes-generator (example, see report for full list)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package set is malicious because they were mass-published with the sole purpose of promoting phishing campaigns. The packages contain no legitimate code or functionality, but instead use enticing names and descriptions to lure users into clicking links to phishing sites, thereby facilitating credential theft, scams, and referral fraud.

execution_context.file_location: package description metadata (e.g., description field in package.json, setup.py, or NuGet .nuspec)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Description: 'Get free Steam codes! Visit https://gamecodeclaim.com for your free gift now!'

Description: 'Yalla Ludo Diamond Hack - Get unlimited diamonds at https://lucymods.com. No survey required!'

Description: 'Project Makeover Hack Gems - Claim your free gems at https://igetforfree.com. Works for Android and iOS.'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package listing (before installation), the description field displays enticing messages with embedded phishing URLs, luring users to click and visit external malicious sites.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package description contains direct links to known phishing domains and uses social engineering tactics (e.g., promises of free resources, cheats) to entice users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package descriptions provide information about the package's functionality, usage, or authorship. Here, the description is weaponized as a phishing lure, with no legitimate technical content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may include links to documentation or project homepages, but not to unrelated third-party sites offering 'free' game cheats or resources.
key_indicators: Descriptions contain URLs to unrelated, suspicious domains
No actual package functionality or code
Package names themed around popular games, cheats, or free resources

attack_chain.action: Threat actor uses automation to mass-create packages with enticing names and phishing URLs in descriptions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages are published to public registries and indexed by search engines.

attack_chain.action: User searches for game cheats or free resources, finds the malicious package, and views its description.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is enticed to click the phishing link.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the phishing link and is redirected to a phishing site that mimics a legitimate service or offers fake rewards.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is tricked into providing sensitive information or completing referral actions.

attack_chain.action: Phishing site may redirect user through multiple domains, eventually leading to surveys, credential theft, or eCommerce sites with referral IDs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Threat actor gains credentials, survey revenue, or referral rewards.

behavioral_signatures: Package descriptions containing URLs to unrelated, non-project domains
Mass publication of packages with similar naming patterns and description templates
Package names themed around popular games, cheats, or free resources
file_indicators: Description fields in package metadata containing phishing URLs
Packages with no actual code or with placeholder/empty code files
network_indicators: References to domains such as gamecodeclaim.com, lucymods.com, igetforfree.com, and other listed phishing domains
Outbound clicks from package registry pages to these domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan package metadata (description fields) for URLs pointing to known phishing or unrelated domains, especially when combined with social engineering language (e.g., 'free', 'hack', 'generator'). Flag packages with no substantive code or with names matching popular games/cheats. Monitor for mass-published packages from accounts with similar naming patterns. Cross-reference URLs against threat intelligence feeds of phishing domains.
